body.headline: Apple is Now the Top-Performing Magnificent 7 Stock in 2026. Here’s why it’s Beating NVIDIA, Tesla, and Amazon
body.summary: Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) has emerged as the best-performing Magnificent Seven stock of 2026, outperforming NVIDIA (NVDA), Microsoft (MSFT), Amazon (AMZN), Alphabet (GOOGL), Meta Platforms (META), and Tesla (TSLA). But what's driving Apple's surprising rally while other AI stocks struggle? In this episode, 24/7 Wall St.'s Eric Bleeker examines why Apple shares have surged more than 27% in 2026, even as concerns about artificial intelligence spending are weighing on some of the market's biggest technology companies. While competitors are committing hundreds of billions of dollars to AI data centers, Apple is taking a different approach. Its strategy emphasizes on-device artificial intelligence, privacy, and integrating AI directly into its ecosystem, avoiding much of the enormous infrastructure spending burden facing its rivals. Eric breaks down Apple's latest earnings, its massive share repurchase program, and why investors are increasingly rewarding the company's capital-efficient AI strategy. He also compares the Magnificent Seven's performance in 2026 against their remarkable returns since the beginning of 2023, revealing a very different picture of the AI investment boom. Has Apple become the market's ultimate AI safe-haven stock? And could its strategy continue outperforming NVIDIA and the rest of Big Tech?

body.headline: Elon Musk Has a Tesla Problem He Can’t Seem to Fix
body.summary: Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) has been one of the most remarkable wealth creators in stock market history. But with Tesla shares falling roughly 20% this year, investors are beginning to ask a difficult question: Has Wall Street finally lost patience with Elon Musk? In this episode, 24/7 Wall St. co-founder Doug McIntyre joins senior writer and editor Lee Jackson to discuss why Tesla is dramatically underperforming many of its Magnificent Seven peers, and whether the company's biggest problem is Elon Musk himself. For years, Musk has argued that Tesla is much more than an electric vehicle manufacturer. He has promised revolutionary advances in artificial intelligence, humanoid robotics, autonomous driving, and robotaxis. Yet many of those promises have taken far longer to materialize than investors expected. Doug explains why Tesla's extraordinary valuation may be increasingly difficult to justify if investors begin treating it primarily as an automotive company rather than an emerging AI powerhouse. The discussion also explores Tesla's electric vehicle sales, its popularity in California, the impact of gasoline prices, growing skepticism surrounding Musk's ambitious timelines, and what upcoming third-quarter earnings could mean for TSLA shareholders. Is Tesla still one of the market's greatest growth stories, or has the Elon Musk premium finally started to disappear?
